source.title: MIB: A Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark
source.authors: Aaron Mueller; Atticus Geiger; Sarah Wiegreffe; Dana Arad; Iv'an Arcuschin; Adam Belfki; Yik Siu Chan; Jaden Fiotto-Kaufman; Tal Haklay; Michael Hanna; Jing Huang; Rohan Gupta; Yaniv Nikankin; Hadas Orgad; Nikhil Prakash; Anja Reusch; A. page_placements.theme: Head roles resolve into finer features and directions

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses causal-variable alignment and interchange interventions, rather than the original circuit-discovery and faithfulness/completeness/minimality evaluation. It tests whether token and position information in GPT-2's identified S-inhibition heads can be disentangled.
record.gate_note: The IOI accuracy figures are task-performance context, not evidence about the circuit, so they are not rows. Results cited from Wang et al. (2023) are also excluded. The IOI-specific results recorded below are the paper's own interchange-intervention alignment MSEs.
record.test_reason: MIB is a benchmark paper. Its IOI causal-variable section repeats Wang et al.'s App. A intervention: S1/S2 flip counterfactuals on the four S-inhibition heads in GPT-2 small, followed by a regression of logit difference on position and token signals. It then adds DAS/DBM disentangling of the two signals. This tests one sub-part of V1, the role of the S-inhibition heads, on a new dataset. The circuit-localization track benchmarks discovery methods by faithfulness curves (CMD/CPR). It does not compare the discovered circuits with the Wang et al. circuit, so that track tests no version directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right for the IOI section. The authors find the subject position and token signals in the four S-inhibition heads can be disentangled. A head-level split works (position in 7.3/7.9/8.6, token in 8.10), but feature-level alignment, especially DAS, does better. Their replicated regression also shows position outweighs token. The paper's overall conclusions concern methods: EAP-IG-inputs is best for circuit localization, and DAS is best for causal variable localization while SAEs are no better than neurons.
record.recipe_differences: Uses causal-variable feature alignment and interchange interventions with MSE, rather than circuit discovery and faithfulness/completeness/minimality evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: IOI alignment MSE differs by causal variable, feature-alignment method, and selected head subset.

fits_no_version.finding: The full-vector brute-force search finds position best aligned to heads 7.3, 7.9 and 8.6 (MSE 2.45) and token to head 8.10 (MSE 2.82). DAS on features of the four heads disentangles the two signals further (MSE 2.20 / 2.08).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within the IOI S-inhibition heads, the subject-position and subject-token signals are carried separably: by different heads, and by different subspaces within heads.

fits_no_version.finding: Circuit-track CMD on IOI GPT-2 (public test) depends on the ablation used for discovery: EAP with mean ablation 0.29, counterfactual 0.03, optimal ablation 0.30; random 0.75. EActP and EAP-IG reach 0.02–0.03.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Faithfulness of method-discovered IOI circuits in GPT-2 depends on the ablation type used for discovery, with counterfactual ablations giving the most faithful circuits.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), 2025; PMLR 267
record.problems: The IOI analysis is limited to GPT-2 and the previously identified S-inhibition heads. The study does not report uncertainty for the IOI MSEs and does not assess the full 26-head circuit or its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality.

untested.parts: The full 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality. Only the S-inhibition heads' position and token signals are tested.
Backup name-mover heads and self-repair after ablation.

The same head classes in other models, sizes or checkpoints, and reuse for other tasks. The causal-variable baselines for IOI run on GPT-2 only. Circuit-track circuits in Qwen, Gemma and Llama are not compared with the Wang et al. head classes.
Whether other discovery methods recover the Wang et al. circuit. The circuit track scores faithfulness curves and never measures overlap with that circuit.
Sensitivity of the Wang et al. circuit's faithfulness to ablation, metric or distribution. Ablation-type sensitivity is shown only for method-discovered circuits.
Name orders, template variants or more names. The 43 templates are pooled and no per-template breakdown is given.

missing.what: The linear regression of logit difference on position and token signals after intervening on the four S-inhibition heads: 0.048 + 2.005·Position + 0.768·Token. It replicates Wang et al.'s 2.31/0.99.

record.verdict_notes: This is a benchmark paper; IOI is one of its tasks. Only the App. F.5.4 replication bears on the claim. The MSEs lack a null baseline and uncertainty, so the record's rows cannot carry a verdict; the verdict rests on the regression text. Table 3(d) full-vector values equal the selected brute-force alignments in Table 18, so r5/r8 duplicate r9/r36.

versions.untested_parts: Tests token and position signals in the four identified S-inhibition heads using causal-variable alignment. Does not test the complete 26-head, 7-class circuit or its faithfulness, completeness, or minimality criteria.
Backup-head takeover after ablating main name-mover heads.
The same circuit in other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks, and component reuse across tasks.
Whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics recover essentially the same circuit.
Sensitivity of circuit faithfulness or completeness to ablation, metric, and prompt distribution, or the fraction of behaviour explained by the circuit.
The same circuit across name orders, templates, and prompts with more names. The IOI counterfactuals vary subject token and position, not these prompt-format dimensions.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small, the four S-inhibition heads (7.3, 7.9, 8.6, 8.10), MIB IOI dataset with IO↔S1/S2 flip counterfactuals
relationships.reason: From the text (App. F.5.4; no row records it): the regression on the four heads gives logit difference ≈ 0.048 + 2.005·Position + 0.768·Token. This matches Wang et al.'s 2.31/0.99, with position dominant, so the heads carry both signals.
relationships.display_finding: Regression yielded logit difference ≈ 0.048 + 2.005·Position + 0.768·Token, resembling the original coefficients of 2.31 and 0.99 and showing stronger position dependence.

relation.reason: The replicated intervention regression provides its own evidence about the signals carried by the four S-inhibition heads.

tranche.reason: Replicates the original signal interventions and adds causal-variable alignment methods to test the position and token mechanisms in the identified S-inhibition heads.

source_check.notes: The statement correctly describes the authors' selected head alignment; Table 18 nevertheless gives STok MSE 2.80 for head 7.9 alone, below 2.82 for 8.10, so 8.10 is not the independently optimal token subset. Appendix F.5.4 also describes the logit-difference sign inconsistently with §4.6.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 IOI causal-variable alignment on the identified S-inhibition heads
reader_labels.reason: Interchange-intervention MSE results provide evidence for disentangling subject-position and subject-token signals in the identified heads; see r1–r36. This supports only the tested signal roles, not the full circuit claim.
